title.value: The Problematizing Review: A Counterpoint to Elsbach and Van Knippenberg's Argument for Integrative Reviews

key_findings.statement: Integrative reviews rest on questionable assumptions: treating the domain as given, privileging hegemonic concepts, following a jigsaw-puzzle accumulation logic, and assuming author neutrality.

The authors propose 'problematizing review' as an alternative built on four principles: (1) reflexivity, (2) reading broadly but selectively, (3) not accumulating but problematizing, (4) less is more.
Problematizing reviews are 'opening up' exercises rather than 'building exercises', aiming to generate new ways of thinking rather than summarising existing knowledge.
